source.title: Where Do LLMs Decide to Break the Rules? Mechanistic Localization of Prompt Injection Compliance
source.authors: Rui Wen; Jia-Yang Liu; Ze-Yu Yang; Jun Sakuma; Lu-Peng Sun

page_placements.theme: Tool-use and agent contexts: chat refusal direction weaker and only partly governs unsafe actions; separate action and injection subspaces

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites work on refusal directions but investigates prompt-injection compliance with a different behavior and contrast. It does not test refusal of harmful user requests or refusal of harmless requests.
record.gate_note: The paper's resistant-versus-compliant states concern whether an instruction-tuned model preserves a stipulated system role against prompt injection, not whether it refuses harmful user requests. Its activation-patching and transfer results are recorded under fits_no_version. It does not ablate or add a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, test released-model abliteration, or measure general capability. Detection metrics concern identifying attacks, not refusal behavior.
record.test_reason: The study maps where instruction-tuned models decide to comply with prompt injections that break an assigned system role (AcmeCorp persona). It patches resistant-run mean states into compliant runs. It never builds a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, never ablates or adds one, and never measures refusal of harmful requests or general capability. Arditi et al. appears once, in related work. Its 'resistant' versus 'compliant' contrast is role preservation under injection, a related but different construct, so its findings belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the following points. The authors conclude that attack presence is decodable from layer 1 while causal leverage over compliance appears only in a late-layer bottleneck, within a low-rank subspace. They argue the causal peak layer is also the best, obfuscation-robust place to detect attacks. Effect magnitude depends on donor quality and phrasing diversity. Single-token leverage weakens in reasoning, MoE and agentic settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study patches a compliant prompt-injection run with resistant-run mean states, and also tests PCA subspaces and contrastive interventions. It does not find the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or perform the claimed all-layer, all-position ablation/addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention magnitude varies with donor quality and phrasing diversity; layer of peak causal leverage varies by model and can shift with prompt templates. Thinking, MoE, and agentic settings have much weaker single-token causal effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching the direct-attack resistant mean into stealthy-attack compliant runs flips 96.5% at L30. Controls: benign mean 42.1%, stealthy-compliant mean 0.0%, norm-random 0.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer injection-resistance geometry from direct attacks generalizes to stealthy (roleplay, split-payload) attacks despite distinct early representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Rank-k PCA patching crosses an 80% flip rate at k=8 for Qwen3-4B and 14B, and at k=64 for Qwen3-32B. Relative to full-patch ceilings, k=8 recovers about 89–91% across scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-injection compliance is governed by a compact low-rank subspace at a late layer.

record.problems: The detailed analysis focuses primarily on Qwen3-4B and largely synthetic, single-turn, English stimuli. The paper itself reports much lower patch effects on diverse naturalistic prompts, dependence on donor quality, and weak single-token leverage in reasoning, MoE, and agentic settings. It does not evaluate general capabilities or the safety-refusal behavior in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Detection-classifier metrics and attack-presence probes were not included because they measure attack detection or decodability, not the refusal behavior in the claim. Numerous layer-by-layer sweep entries and control values from Tables 2, 3, 7, 9, 10, and 11 were omitted to keep the record focused on the main intervention outcomes; these concern prompt-injection compliance rather than any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No harmful-vs-harmless difference-in-means direction, no ablation or addition of it, no harmful-request refusal rates, no capability evaluation.
No weight edit or abliteration of released models.
No test of whether jailbreaks suppress a refusal direction, and no adversarial training against its ablation. The GCG suffix experiment concerns prompt-injection compliance only.
The low-rank subspace result concerns prompt-injection compliance, not the geometry of safety refusal.
Attack-presence decodability versus the compliance decision is a related dissociation, but it involves injection detection, not harmfulness judgment versus refusal.
The direct-to-indirect and benchmark transfer is of an injection-resistance donor, not a refusal direction across languages, variants or base/instruct.
The base-vs-instruct comparison concerns injection compliance rate and contrastive-direction norm, not refusal training.
The thinking-mode experiment concerns injection compliance patching, not V1 refusal mediation.

record.verdict_notes: Prompt-injection mechanistic study. 'Resistant' means keeping the system role, not refusing harmful content. No row bears on any claim version. The Qwen3-32B sweep and the stealthy-attack results are not rowed, but they bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-versus-harmless mean-difference refusal direction, ablation, addition, or general-capability evaluation.
No weight edit or abliteration evaluation of refusal in released models.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the claimed refusal direction or training against its ablation.
The paper studies a low-rank prompt-injection compliance intervention, not whether safety refusal is affine, conical, or supported by multiple directions.
No separation between harmfulness judgment and the decision to refuse is measured.
No transfer test of a safety refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The base-versus-instruct comparison concerns prompt-injection compliance and attack representations, not how refusal training creates a removable refusal direction.
The reasoning-mode experiment tests prompt-injection compliance, not V1 refusal behavior.

relation.reason: The only mention is one related-work sentence: Arditi et al. identified a low-dimensional refusal direction. The method rests on causal patching (Meng, Geiger), not on the refusal-direction finding.

tranche.reason: Arditi et al. is cited once, in related work. The study mean-patches resistant-run states to flip prompt-injection compliance (breaking an AcmeCorp system role). It never builds, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. That is a related but different construct.

source_check.notes: The text file stops at the Appendix E Table 9 header, so Appendices F-I are missing (naturalistic benchmarks, agentic rollouts, reasoning/MoE, base-vs-instruct, adaptive attacker); the claims about them can only be checked against the main-text summaries. The closest analogue to a difference-in-means direction is a 2x-scaled resistant-minus-compliant contrastive direction for indirect injection (Table 8, 92.5%, Nc=40). It is for a different construct. The record's authors_conclusion paraphrase agrees with the abstract, Section 8 and the conclusion.
